Title: Effectiveness of an application-based neck exercise as a pain management tool for office workers with chronic neck pain and functional disability: A pilot randomized trial
Author: JaeHyuk Lee et al.
Comment: The paper does not report a standardized effect size. Hedges g was computed from the explicitly reported 8-week arm means, SDs, and sample sizes, oriented so positive values favor app-based exercise: control minus intervention because lower VAS indicates less pain. M_diff = 3.69 - 2.73 = 0.96 mm; SE_diff was computed as sqrt(1.99^2/11 + 2.02^2/9) = 0.9002 mm; pooled-SD Cohen d = 0.4792 and small-sample-corrected Hedges g = 0.459. The reported P = 0.02 is from the Mann-Whitney U test comparing pre-post improvement amounts, whereas the computed standardized effect uses post-intervention arm-level data; the U statistic and change-score SDs were not reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('App-based exercise group') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: workplace environment at Korea University Graduate School
Content length: approximately 10–15 min/day, at least 2 days/week, for 8 weeks
Topic of Content: McKenzie neck exercise for chronic neck pain
interaction_type: self-directed app-based exercise with self-feedback; both arms received weekly pain-care text messages
Participant type: office workers aged 25–35 years with neck pain for more than 6 months
Outcome measurement: Current pain on a Visual Analog Scale from 0 mm (no pain) to 100 mm (unbearable pain)

Title: The effectiveness of telerehabilitation-based structured exercise therapy for chronic nonspecific neck pain: A randomized controlled trial
Author: Merve Özel and Pınar Kaya Ciddi
Comment: The paper reports post-therapy arm means and 95% CIs but not SDs. No standardized effect was computed. The sentence-level p < 0.001 covers the three-group post-therapy comparison rather than an explicitly quantified isolated RSG-versus-CG test, so it was not entered. The eligible pairwise arm data were extracted without using the active RSG-versus-UG contrast or an omnibus statistic.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Remote supervised group (RSG)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); treatment SD derived from its reported mean CI; control SD derived from its reported mean CI
Medium: Weekly exercise videos and brochures delivered by email, with individual Zoom videoconference supervision and text-message monitoring
Content length: Four-week exercise program; videos less than 10 min; eight approximately 40-min videoconference sessions planned
Topic of Content: Progressive structured stretching, strengthening, stabilization, and proprioceptive exercises
interaction_type: Synchronous videoconference supervision plus asynchronous video, brochure, email, and text-message delivery/monitoring
Participant type: Adults with chronic nonspecific neck pain for at least 3 months
Recruitment source: Announcements on social media and WhatsApp groups; volunteers contacted the researchers by phone and email
Outcome measurement: Current pain rated on the Numerical Pain Rating Scale over 10 points, where 0 reflects no pain and 10 reflects the worst pain score

Title: Effects of Interactive Telerehabilitation Practices in Office Workers with Chronic Nonspecific Neck Pain: Randomized Controlled Study
Author: Özlü et al.
Comment: Only post-treatment medians and IQRs are reported for the isolated eligible arms; means and SDs are unavailable, so Cohen’s d/Hedges g, M_diff, and SE_diff cannot be validly calculated. The reported post-treatment p<0.001 is an omnibus three-group Kruskal–Wallis result and was not extracted as the Group 1 versus Group 3 pairwise p value. Group 2 was excluded because it was an active exercise comparator. The arm-specific medians are consistent with the stated direction of effect.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group 1: interactive telerehabilitation exercises plus office ergonomics training') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); mean/SD estimated from median/IQR via Wan et al. (2014): treatment mean=5.2500 SD=0.7689, control mean=7.3125 SD=1.3456 -- APPROXIMATION, not directly reported
Study Environment: Office workers recruited through outpatient clinics; intervention delivered remotely in participants’ own setting
Medium: Interactive online application with live video connection
Content length: 45 min per day, 3 days a week, for 6 weeks
Topic of Content: Strengthening, motor-control, posture-correction, cervical range-of-motion, and stretching exercises
interaction_type: Live interactive supervision and verbal correction by a physiotherapist
Participant type: Office workers aged 18–45 years with chronic nonspecific neck pain, working more than 35 hours per week at a desk or computer
Recruitment source: Outpatient clinics of Kutahya Health Science University Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Department
Outcome measurement: Pain intensity during movement measured using a 10 cm visual analog scale, with 0=no pain and 10=unbearable pain
additional_group_ns: Group 2: n=40; excluded from the planned pairwise synthesis because it received an active home exercise program

Report_ID: Mean neck pain intensity during the first 3 months based on daily NRS measurements
Title: App-Based Relaxation Exercises for Patients With Chronic Neck Pain: Pragmatic Randomized Trial
Author: Pach et al.
Comment: The outcome is an average of daily pain measurements across the first 3 months, not a point measurement exactly at 3 months. Table 2 reports adjusted means and states adjustment for sex and baseline value. Arm-level SDs are not reported, so Cohen d and Hedges g cannot be calculated. The reported raw difference is intervention minus control; because lower NRS values are better, 0.3 points numerically favors control and would require sign reorientation for a synthesis in which positive values favor telerehabilitation.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('App-based intervention') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); ANOVA: missing F-value or group sizes
Study Environment: Single-center pragmatic self-care study with intervention and follow-up delivered/collected through participants' smartphones
Medium: Smartphone app with audio-based relaxation exercises
Topic of Content: Autogenic training, mindfulness meditation, and guided imagery for chronic neck pain
Participant type: Adults aged 18-65 years with chronic neck pain lasting more than 12 weeks
Recruitment source: Universities, gyms, general practitioners' offices, and local subway advertising in Berlin
Outcome measurement: Numeric Rating Scale (0=no pain to 10=worst possible pain); mean daily neck pain intensity during the first 3 months
Outcome variable: Mean neck pain intensity during the first 3 months based on daily NRS measurements
